correctness.rationale: For every fixed interior parameter, all transition and stationary probabilities are positive. Uniform conditioning of at most two Markov coordinates bounds representation failure geometrically in the fringe length. The algebraic increment of the fringe score vanishes when each of three sums at the new index occurs. Path-weight ratios on a sufficiently small complex polydisc cost at most exp(epsilon K), outweighed by the geometric real rare-event bound. Normal convergence of rational finite-fringe probabilities gives holomorphy; Cauchy yields all derivative limits. Existing fringe-middle probability estimates plus mixing link this analytic limit to the original arithmetic densities. The attached exact-rational verifier checks finite identities, not infinite holomorphy.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 source proves existence/positivity, not parameter regularity; its rational expected-gap formula cannot determine the three event probabilities. Full-text comparisons with the 2014 correlated-pair continuity result, Zhao uniform-model theorem and 2011 MSTD survey do not yield the two-variable stationary Markov analyticity theorem. A new complex-uniform rare-change estimate supplies the needed implication. A general unindexed abstract theorem or equivalent derivation remains a risk; database absence alone is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished equivalent result is not excluded.

value.rationale: The new parameter-dependent arithmetic probabilities are the object of a published two-parameter maximization conjecture. Joint interior real analyticity and convergent exact rational derivative approximations enable rigorous gradient/Hessian reasoning, qualitatively stronger than source positivity/existence and earlier continuity in another model. The complex finite-energy argument is necessary: uniform convergence of real-analytic finite probabilities on the real square would not suffice. No maximizer or boundary behavior is claimed.
